rv.q: Tang’s production isn’t perfect by a long chalk: in a theatre designed for different states of candlelight she lets harsh artificial illumination overwhelm the flames.
This is a witty production that finds an interesting new slant of power struggle inflected by gender.
As the revelations and explanations arrive one after the other, Tang and company make the story’s contradictions something to celebrate.
Maybe it is lesser performed for good reason, or perhaps this production, full of inspired ideas, does not anchor them down enough.
The sprawling play displays its customary capacity to snare attention; we allow the far-fetched flourishes while the drops of heartfelt speech (“Hang there, like fruit, my soul…”) work a treat.
They give depth and flavour to a mediocre script.
She has a solid grasp of a slippery play.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet Jennifer Tang's gender-swapped Cymbeline. The bold matriarchal reimagining earns praise, but Shakespeare's notoriously tangled plot divides critics between admiring the production's ambition and questioning whether the unwieldy source material ever fully coher
